parsed.why: Direct cross-dressing criminalisation up to 6 years; police raids, anal exams, arrests; hostile social violence, despite court freezes. Outed trans visitor faces severe state punishment and abuse.

No trans criminalisation; courts decriminalised, Pride exists. Immigration lists homosexuals and religious hostility persist, but no documented anti-trans targeting; outed visitor faces friction, not severe punishment.

No trans-specific law; sodomy unenforced; documented traditional gender role suggests tolerance. Thin data lacks current social evidence, but no documented targeting or visitor-facing ban lowers consequences.

Trans status not criminalised; institutions are partly trans-respecting. But male-marker border stops raise discovery, and historical police tolerance of anti-LGBT violence leaves moderate harassment risk if outed.

Transgender people face section 377, police Act detention, rape, stripping parades, torture and killings intensified after coup; no working remedy. Outed visitor faces arbitrary custody and life-threatening abuse.
